title: Satisfying Real-world Goals with Dataset Constraints
authors: Gabriel Goh, Andrew Cotter, Maya Gupta, Michael P. Friedlander
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS/NIPS), Vol. 29
conclusions: Proposes 'dataset constraints': training a linear classifier subject to upper/lower bounds on positive/negative prediction RATES computed on specified (possibly unlabeled) datasets, covering coverage, churn/stability, fairness, and recall/precision goals in one framework.

Replaces the discontinuous 0/1-based rate with the bounded ramp function sigma(z)=max{0,min{1,1/2+z}}, then solves the resulting non-convex problem via a majorization-minimization procedure that iteratively builds tight convex (hinge/constant) upper bounds.
The convex subproblems are solved via a Lagrangian/cutting-plane scheme (Algorithm 2) reducing to repeated weighted-SVM training, since the ramp bound reduces to an SVM-style objective.
Fairness experiment (Adult/a9a dataset): constrains male vs female positive-rate ratio, beating Zafar et al. 2015's covariance-constraint baseline at every fairness ratio.

Churn experiment (proprietary Google UI dataset): constrains churn/recall of a new classifier relative to a deployed one on a large unlabeled dataset D3, showing lower churn than a thresholded-SVM baseline at matched accuracy.

Frames its own constraints as bounding expected/rate quantities meant to generalize inductively to new data (explicit train/test generalization discussion, Appendix C), not as hard exact-count guarantees verified on one fixed known test set.
our_use: main.tex:181 cites it as the exemplar of controlling 'coverage (the fraction of items predicted positive) as a dataset constraint', grouped under the 'Rate-constrained learning' related-work paragraph alongside eban2017scalable, cotter2019optimization, narasimhan2019optimizing; text then contrasts these as bounding 'expected rates over a distribution, inductively' versus our transductive hard count on one fixed test set.
